precision_basis: Computational arithmetic tolerances only: endpoint1e-12 and coefficient1e-6. No biological effect margin, sample-size or precision claim is inferred.
amendment_reason: The first exposed gain could reflect extra regularization flexibility; this separate bounded diagnostic tests that concrete alternative using unchanged predictor spaces and already saved scores.
question: Does the observed residual-associated paired log-loss gain exceed gains obtainable by duplicating a fixed baseline feature without adding predictor information?
decision: Qualify whether regularization geometry is a sufficient explanation for the first exposed internal gain before attributing incremental biological information to the lesion residual.
strongest_rival: Under fixed L2, correlated or duplicate features distribute coefficients across penalties and can increase predictive confidence even when the linear predictor space is unchanged.
discriminator: Duplicate each of the four baseline columns one at a time, retaining exactly the existing leave-one-patient-out folds, training-only scales and lambda=1 primary/.1/10 sensitivities. Compare all controls directly to the frozen residual result.
exposure_record: The A11 paired-prediction v1 gain and all patients being correctly ordered were inspected before this diagnostic. The control calculations remain unexecuted at freeze. This is an exposed qualification amendment, not confirmation.
biological_unit: Eight source-supported paired patients; each contains normal-AT2 and author-labelled tumour epithelial pseudobulks.
nesting_and_overlap: Cells form pseudobulks nested in samples and patients. Eight folds share training patients and are not independent model-training experiments. This reuses the original Kim cohort.
population_and_selection: Exactly the saved eight patient pairs and fixed shared_remodelling/p53/hypoxia/inflammatory-response scores from g1_a11_paired_prediction_v1. No raw reprocessing, new gene, new biological score or sample selection.
contrast: Same four-feature baseline versus the same baseline with one of its four columns duplicated; compare each five-column control to the existing five-column lesion-augmented model. Display all four controls, all three penalties and all eight patients.
endpoint: Equal-patient mean held-out paired log loss and control gain over baseline; lesion gain relative to each duplicate control. Counts of patients better under each control remain descriptive.
methods: Reuse the frozen fit function and saved per-library scores. Train-only scaling and paired L2 logistic fit with the same optimizer checks. A synthetic test verifies that duplicating a column equals halving that coordinate penalty without expanding the linear predictor space. Independently reconstruct all prior 72 probabilities/losses and six aggregate gains with standard-library arithmetic from saved scores and coefficients; tolerance1e-12.
missingness_and_exclusions: No exclusions or tuning. Fail if the original endpoint arithmetic, optimizer agreement or paired design checks fail. All96 control predictions and12 aggregate comparisons are retained.
multiplicity: All four duplicates are equally reported controls, not biological hypotheses or a search for the most favorable baseline. Lambda=1 stays primary; .1/10 stay sensitivity. No p-values or biological CIs.
interpretation_limit: A duplicate gain is a property of penalty geometry, not biology. Residual superiority over these controls would still be exposed internal measurement evidence, not mechanism, cancer specificity, prospective fate or an independently validated biomarker.
stop_rule: Stop on failed endpoint/coefficient checks. Preserve the original positive result, every control and any ambiguity; do not tune penalties or nominate alternate genes to restore a favored reading.
